#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Waits for the iPad to answer, then copies Manic's crash reports and session logs here.
set -u
. "$HOME/.local/share/ios-signer/scripts/env.sh"
OUT="$(dirname "$0")"
TOOL="$SIGNER_HOME/bin/rpcheck-logs"
BUNDLE="com.globocodes.manicemu"
deadline=$(( $(date +%s) + 6*3600 ))
while [ "$(date +%s)" -lt "$deadline" ]; do
    host="$(signer_find_ipad 2>/dev/null || true)"
    if [ -n "$host" ]; then
        echo "$(date -Is) iPad answers on $host"
        "$TOOL" "$host" "$IPAD_PAIRING" crashlogs ManicEmu > "$OUT/crashlogs.txt" 2> "$OUT/crashlogs.err" || { cat "$OUT/crashlogs.err"; }
        cat "$OUT/crashlogs.txt"
        grep -v '^pairing\|^tunnel' "$OUT/crashlogs.txt" | awk -F'\t' '$2=="S_IFREG"{print $1}' | tail -12 | while read -r name; do
            "$TOOL" "$host" "$IPAD_PAIRING" crashpull "$name" "$OUT/$name" 2>&1 | tail -1
        done
        "$TOOL" "$host" "$IPAD_PAIRING" docs-ls "$BUNDLE" "/Documents/Netplay Logs" > "$OUT/netplay-logs.txt" 2> "$OUT/netplay-logs.err" || { cat "$OUT/netplay-logs.err"; }
        cat "$OUT/netplay-logs.txt"
        "$TOOL" "$host" "$IPAD_PAIRING" docs-pull "$BUNDLE" "/Documents/Netplay Logs/Manic MP sessions.log" "$OUT/Manic MP sessions.log" 2>&1 | tail -1
        grep -v '^pairing\|^tunnel' "$OUT/netplay-logs.txt" | awk -F'\t' '$2=="S_IFREG" && $1!="Manic MP sessions.log"{print $4"\t"$1}' | sort | tail -4 | cut -f2 | while read -r name; do
            "$TOOL" "$host" "$IPAD_PAIRING" docs-pull "$BUNDLE" "/Documents/Netplay Logs/$name" "$OUT/$name" 2>&1 | tail -1
        done
        echo "$(date -Is) pull finished"
        exit 0
    fi
    sleep 60
done
echo "$(date -Is) gave up: iPad never answered"
exit 3
EOF
chmod +x $S/ipad-pull/watch-and-pull.sh; echo written; $S/ipad-pull/watch-and-pull.sh

payload.text:
Root cause found from the iPad's own crash report, and the fix is in place awaiting your ship go-ahead.

**What crashed.** The Shrek 2 launch on Oct 16 at 23:42 died on Dolphin's CPU thread with a bus error. The kernel refused to execute the very first block of Dolphin's JIT code buffer as unsigned code. The report carries the sticky "has been debugged" flag, and the code region was mapped read-execute, so Manic believed JIT was fine.

**Why it only happens sometimes.** Your iPad is TXM-class hardware on iPadOS 26. There, JIT only works while StikDebug is actually attached, because the core asks the attached debugger to make each JIT region executable. StikDebug had attached at app launch at 23:36, then got suspended or killed in the background. The game started 6.5 minutes later. The fork's JIT check only looked at the sticky flag, which never clears after the debugger leaves, so Dolphin booted on JIT with nobody to grant it. A fresh app launch re-attaches StikDebug and works, which is what made it look random. The Animal Crossing session you started right after the crash ran fine for exactly that reason.

**The fix.**
- RetroArch fork, new branch `game-start-crash` (pushed, pin moved to it): on TXM hardware JIT availability now also requires a live tracer, read via the process flags. PPL devices keep the old behaviour. A new "JIT debugger detached" query is exposed to the app.
- App: when a game asks for JIT but the debugger is gone, a toast says "JIT is off for this session: StikDebug is no longer attached" and the session runs the interpreter instead of crashing. One new string in every language file.
- Bonus fix for a second definite crash I hit while tracing: changing a GameCube or Wii game's platform ran a Realm write inside another write, which throws an uncatchable exception. Writes now join an open transaction.

**Caveats.** No Xcode on the Pi, so this is unbuilt; the CI workflow compiles it. The iPad runs the `build/ac-events` branch, not main, so the fix needs a merge there after the PR lands. I armed two follow-ups for that moment: merge main into `build/ac-events`, then pull and sign the build onto the iPad.

**Also new.** The Pi can now fetch crash reports and Manic's session logs straight off the iPad over the signer's tunnel. The tool is `~/.local/share/ios-signer/bin/rpcheck-logs` with its source kept beside the signer; it should eventually fold into the better-games signer repo. The signer's existing tool is untouched.

## What

Fixes the intermittent crash when starting a GameCube/Wii game (last seen with Shrek 2 on 2026-10-16 23:42).

**Root cause.** On TXM-class hardware running iOS 26 (A15+/M2+, e.g. the iPad Air M4), JIT pages only execute while a debugger is attached: the core asks the attached debugger, via `brk`, to make each JIT region executable. StikDebug attaches at app launch and is often suspended or killed in the background before a game starts. `CS_DEBUGGED` is sticky, so `jit_available()` kept reporting JIT as usable, the `brk` request was silently skipped by the app's own SIGTRAP handler, and Dolphin's first JIT block executed from an unsigned page: `EXC_BAD_ACCESS` / `KERN_CODESIGN_ERROR` on the CPU thread at the dual-mapped JIT buffer. A fresh app launch re-attaches StikDebug, which is why it looked random.

## Changes

- **Dependencies/Libretro** → `game-start-crash` (globocodes/RetroArch `3bf884a8`). On TXM hardware `jit_available()` now also requires a live tracer (`P_TRACED` via `sysctl KERN_PROC`), so the core runs the interpreter when the debugger is gone. PPL devices keep the old behaviour. New `jit_debugger_detached()` / `+[LibretroCore JITDebuggerDetached]`.
- **PlayViewController** (`SIDE_LOAD` only): when the game asks for JIT but the debugger has detached, a 6 s toast explains that JIT is off for this session and how to get it back.
- **Localizable.strings**: new `JITDebuggerDetached` key in all 37 locales (English text, as the existing sideload strings do).
- **ObjectUpdatable.change**: joins an already-open Realm write instead of nesting one. `PlatformSelectionView` calls `ensureDolphinGameID()` inside its own `realm.write`, and nested writes throw an uncatchable `RLMException`.

## Verification

- Diagnosed from the iPad's own crash report (`codeSigningFlags` includes `CS_DEBUGGED`, `codeSigningMonitor=2`, fault at the Dolphin JIT buffer) and Manic's session log (`JITARM64 · JIT on` for the crashing start; later interpreter sessions of the same game ran fine).
- Not compiled locally (no Xcode on the Pi); `build-sideload.yml` builds it.
- The installed iPad build comes from `build/ac-events`, so this needs merging there after landing; follow-ups are armed for that.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Copy Manic's crash reports and session logs from the iPad into a directory.
# Read-only on the device: nothing is installed, deleted or paired.
#
#   manic-logs.sh <out dir> [--wait <minutes>] [--reports <n>] [--logs <n>]
#
#   --wait     keep trying for this long until the iPad answers (default 0: one try)
#   --reports  how many of the newest Manic crash reports to copy (default 12)
#   --logs     how many of the newest per-session RetroArch logs to copy (default 4)
#
# What lands in <out dir>:
#   crashlogs.txt            every report the device keeps whose name contains ManicEmu
#   <report>.ips             the newest --reports of them
#   netplay-logs.txt         the listing of Documents/Netplay Logs
#   Manic MP sessions.log    one line per game session: title, core, run mode
#   retroarch__*.log         the newest --logs per-session RetroArch logs
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")"
. ./env.sh

out="${1:?output directory}"; shift
wait_min=0; n_reports=12; n_logs=4
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
    case "$1" in
        --wait) wait_min="${2:?--wait needs minutes}"; shift 2 ;;
        --reports) n_reports="${2:?--reports needs a count}"; shift 2 ;;
        --logs) n_logs="${2:?--logs needs a count}"; shift 2 ;;
        *) echo "usage: $0 <out dir> [--wait <minutes>] [--reports <n>] [--logs <n>]" >&2; exit 2 ;;
    esac
done
mkdir -p "$out"

tool="$SIGNER_HOME/bin/rpcheck"
bundle="com.globocodes.manicemu"
logdir="/Documents/Netplay Logs"

deadline=$(( $(date +%s) + wait_min*60 ))
host=""
while :; do

    [ -n "$host" ] && break
    if [ "$(date +%s)" -ge "$deadline" ]; then
        echo "iPad not reachable on any of: $IPAD_HOSTS, nor by its hardware address" >&2
        exit 1
    fi
    sleep 60
done
echo "iPad: $host"

# rpcheck prints its pairing/tunnel progress lines first; the listing rows are tab separated.
rows() { grep -v '^pairing\|^tunnel' "$1" | awk -F'\t' -v kind="$2" '$2==kind'; }

"$tool" "$host" "$IPAD_PAIRING" crashlogs ManicEmu > "$out/crashlogs.txt"
echo "crash reports: $(rows "$out/crashlogs.txt" S_IFREG | wc -l) (listing in crashlogs.txt)"
rows "$out/crashlogs.txt" S_IFREG | cut -f1 | sort | tail -n "$n_reports" | while read -r name; do

done

"$tool" "$host" "$IPAD_PAIRING" docs-ls "$bundle" "$logdir" > "$out/netplay-logs.txt"
echo "session logs: $(rows "$out/netplay-logs.txt" S_IFREG | wc -l) (listing in netplay-logs.txt)"
"$tool" "$host" "$IPAD_PAIRING" docs-pull "$bundle" "$logdir/Manic MP sessions.log" "$out/Manic MP sessions.log" | tail -1
# Column 4 is the modification time; take the newest per-session logs.
rows "$out/netplay-logs.txt" S_IFREG | awk -F'\t' '$1!="Manic MP sessions.log"{print $4"\t"$1}' | sort | tail -n "$n_logs" | cut -f2 | while read -r name; do

Both loose ends are done.

**RetroArch fork.** The fork's default branch `master` is only a mirror of upstream RetroArch, so the fix did not belong there. The fork's real integration line is `multiplayer`, which `controller-latency` and then `game-start-crash` were stacked on. I fast-forwarded both `multiplayer` and `controller-latency` to the fix commit, so the ManicEMU pin is now reachable from the fork's working branch and the topic branch is no longer the only holder.

**Signer tool.** The four log-pull arms are now in the better-games signer source as pull request #34:
https://github.com/globocodes/better-games/pull/34

- `rpcheck` gains `crashlogs`, `crashpull`, `docs-ls` and `docs-pull`. No dependency change, so the lock file is untouched and the locked build still passes.
- `ipad.sh` exposes them, and a new `manic-logs.sh` copies Manic's crash reports and session logs into a directory in one command, with an optional wait for the iPad to answer.
- Verified by building in the pinned Rust image and running the full pull against the iPad over the tunnel.
